phrases.text: Competing for more wealth and greater numbers has distracted you, O people, from obeying your Lord and from that which would save you from His anger.

The Prophet said that of your wealth you have only what you have eaten and used up, or worn and worn out, or given away in charity. And he had said before that if the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth he would want a third, and nothing fills his belly but dust.

phrases.translation: until you end up in ˹your˺ graves
phrases.text: Until you went to the graves and were buried in them. Tabari notes that this settles that there is punishment in the grave, for God has told these people, who were distracted by competing for more, that they will learn what awaits them when they visit the graves.

phrases.translation: But no! You will soon come to know
phrases.text: Do not act in this way, that competing for abundance distracts you. You will know, when you visit the graves, what your conduct and your preoccupation with more have brought you.

phrases.translation: Again, no! You will soon come to know
phrases.text: The same thing is said a second time, and Tabari says the Arabs repeated a word twice when they wanted to make a threat heavier. He gives the reading in which the first warning is for the unbelievers and the second for the believers.

phrases.translation: Indeed, if you were to know ˹your fate˺ with certainty,
phrases.text: If you knew with a complete and certain knowledge that God will raise you again after your death, then competing for more would not have distracted you from obeying Him, and you would have hastened to His worship and feared His punishment for your souls.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ you will surely see the Hellfire
phrases.text: You will see the Fire on the day of resurrection with your own eyes, and it will never escape you. The reciters differ over the reading, and Tabari takes the opening vowel in both places.

phrases.translation: Again, you will surely see it with the eye of certainty
phrases.text: And Ibn Abbas said this is said to the polytheists.

phrases.translation: Then, on that Day, you will definitely be questioned about ˹your worldly˺ pleasures
phrases.text: God will question you about the blessings you enjoyed, what you did with them, how you came by them and what you did with them. The commentators differed over what the word means: some said security and health, some said a portion of what a person eats or drinks, and some said everything a person enjoys in this world.

Tabari's own reading covers them all, because God did not name one kind of blessing and rule out another. The exceptions the Prophet named are three: a garment to cover oneself, a morsel to still hunger, and a shelter to get in out of the heat and the cold.
